summary: Comprehensive frontend + backend testing of BlackrodLife prototype. Backend: 5/5 pytest cases pass — health, status CRUD (Mongo persistence), real AI parse-content (Emergent LLM Claude Sonnet 4.5) returning full ParsedSuggestion schema for both event and update inputs. Frontend: All routes load, all critical data-testid attributes present and functional. Theme toggle, role switcher (guest/admin/org/contributor), Events list + Month calendar grid + filters, EventDetail with share/book/google-cal/outlook-cal/apple-cal buttons (note: testids are event-google-cal / event-outlook-cal / event-apple-cal, not cal-google etc. as worded in the request), Organisations directory + profile + follow toggle, Submit Event form (full happy path → toast + success screen), Add Organisation form, Admin dashboard with approve/reject pending items, OrgDashboard AI Upload-Once flow end-to-end (ai-text-input → ai-example-btn fills → ai-parse-btn → real AI returns in ~8s → ai-card-event/social/notif rendered → 'Create event draft' button works), LocalFeed posts, Venues, Volunteering with Under-18/18+ filter, Notifications preference toggles + save.
action_items: Naming clarification only (not a bug): in the original review request the EventDetail calendar buttons were referenced as cal-google/cal-outlook/cal-apple; in code they are event-google-cal/event-outlook-cal/event-apple-cal. Buttons all render correctly and produce a valid Google Calendar TEMPLATE URL. Either keep current names or align with the originally-quoted names — purely a consistency call.
critical_code_review_comments: AppContext stores all CRUD data in memory only — any hard navigation/refresh resets pending events, follows, role, notification prefs, AI drafts. This is expected for a prototype with mock data per the PRD, but every dashboard/admin verification will look broken if a tester reaches it via a direct URL paste instead of in-app navigation. Consider persisting to localStorage so reloads keep state during demos.
/api/parse-content has good resilience (regex fallback when LLM fails/missing key) — solid pattern.
Backend status endpoint correctly excludes _id and reserialises timestamp — no MongoDB ObjectId leakage.
CORS is wide open via CORS_ORIGINS=* — fine for prototype, lock down before production.
Submit-event form: required fields are validated via native HTML5 only; no inline error UI for missing email/venue/desc — acceptable for prototype.
test_credentials: Not applicable — mock auth via role-switcher dropdown (role-guest / role-admin / role-org / role-contributor)
seed_data_creation: None — used existing mock data in /app/frontend/src/data/mockData.js. Backend Mongo only used by /api/status; one TEST_pytest_client status entry was inserted (harmless).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend tests live at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py — covers /api/, /api/status (CRUD + persistence), /api/parse-content (empty/event/update text against real Emergent LLM). Frontend SPA navigation must be used (not page.goto) for any flow that depends on AppContext mutations like 'create event draft → admin pending'. EventDetail calendar testids are event-google-cal / event-outlook-cal / event-apple-cal. OrgDashboard requires role=org (set via role-switcher → role-org). AI generation typically returns within 6–10s — wait up to 60s before failing.
rca of the issue: No bugs found. Single naming inconsistency between the review-request copy and the actual data-testid values for calendar buttons — buttons themselves work correctly and emit a valid Google Calendar TEMPLATE link.
